title: Week 32 Quiz — The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment

questions.prompt: Week 32 · The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment: Which term best matches this definition: A home loan made to a borrower with higher assessed credit risk.
questions.explanation: subprime mortgage is defined in this week as: A home loan made to a borrower with higher assessed credit risk.

questions.prompt: Week 32 · The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment: Which term best matches this definition: Pooling financial assets and selling claims on their cash flows.
questions.explanation: securitization is defined in this week as: Pooling financial assets and selling claims on their cash flows.

questions.prompt: Week 32 · The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment: Which term best matches this definition: Risk that failure in one part of a system can destabilize the whole system.
questions.explanation: systemic risk is defined in this week as: Risk that failure in one part of a system can destabilize the whole system.

questions.prompt: Week 32 · The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment: Which term best matches this definition: Government support intended to prevent collapse of an institution or system.
questions.explanation: bailout is defined in this week as: Government support intended to prevent collapse of an institution or system.

questions.prompt: Week 32 · The Financial Crisis, Recovery, and Political Realignment: Which term best matches this definition: Legal loss of property after failure to meet mortgage obligations.
questions.explanation: foreclosure is defined in this week as: Legal loss of property after failure to meet mortgage obligations.

questions.prompt: What transformed housing losses into systemic financial risk?
choices: A single type of mortgage by itself
Interconnected institutions, securitization, leverage, weak risk controls, falling asset values, and frozen credit
Home prices falling in one neighborhood only
questions.explanation: Systemic crisis emerged through interacting financial mechanisms and institutional connections.

questions.prompt: Why is 'bailout' not by itself a complete evaluation of emergency intervention?
choices: The word identifies neither the systemic risk prevented nor the conditions, distributional effects, and accountability attached to support.
Only private actors can create moral hazard.
questions.explanation: Evaluation requires purpose, beneficiaries, conditions, costs, alternatives, and future incentives.

questions.prompt: How can national recovery and continuing household hardship both be true?
choices: They cannot; one must be false.
Aggregate output and employment can improve while specific households and regions still face foreclosure, lost wealth, or slower recovery.
Household experience is never relevant to economic history.
National statistics measure every family’s condition exactly.
questions.explanation: Aggregate recovery does not imply equal or simultaneous recovery across households and regions.

questions.prompt: Which causal chain best explains credit contraction during the crisis?
choices: Defaults → falling asset values → balance-sheet losses and uncertainty → reduced lending → weaker business and household spending
Higher home prices → guaranteed bank solvency → more lending forever
questions.explanation: The chain traces how financial losses and uncertainty impaired institutional balance sheets and credit availability.

questions.prompt: Which emergency-response design best addresses both systemic stability and accountability?
choices: Provide unlimited support with no conditions.
Allow every interconnected institution to fail simultaneously.
Specify beneficiaries, conditions, loss allocation, transparency, oversight, and measurable stabilization goals.
Judge success only by stock-market performance the next day.
questions.explanation: A defensible response combines stabilization objectives with explicit accountability and evaluation mechanisms.

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: Why did financial risk become a national crisis, and why did recovery produce continuing political anger?
shortResponse.exemplar: A full-credit response states a defensible claim, uses two accurate details, explains how each supports the claim, and acknowledges one complexity or limitation.
